written: 2026-09-25, before any of the new models were trained
status: exploratory; APTOS previously used. Fixes the comparison in advance so it cannot be tuned after the fact.
question: Does changing only the starting weights of a model reduce shared blind spots, and by how much relative to changing the architecture?

models.vit_base_dinov2: vit_base_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m at 224 px, 3 seeds, new (14-pixel patches: recorded caveat)
models.different_architecture_reference: existing EyePACS-trained 5-class DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, ResNet50, RETFound, 3 seeds each

training: EyePACS v2 train split, stabilized ViT recipe identical to TRAIN_eyepacs_v2_VIT_ALLSEEDS; only initialisation differs
evaluation_set: APTOS 2019 (3,662 images), f = 1.31 x referable prevalence, image-level bootstrap (1,000)

outcomes.primary: co-miss ratio for referable disease (grade 2 or worse) by pair type
secondary: co-miss ratio for grade 3 or worse
co-miss ratio for PDR (expected to be sparse)

pair_types.vit_different_init: ViT-Base pairs with different initialisations (supervised vs MAE, supervised vs DINOv2, MAE vs DINOv2), each also reported separately
pair_types.different_architecture_same_data: pairs among the existing non-ViT EyePACS models and between them and ViT-Base supervised

what_counts_as_a_signal: co-miss ratio for vit_different_init clearly below vit_seed_siblings (bootstrap interval of the difference excludes zero). Secondary reading: where vit_different_init falls relative to different_architecture_same_data. If comparable, initialisation rather than architecture drives shared blind spots.
quality_note: Validation and APTOS AUC are reported for every model; if one initialisation is markedly weaker, a partner-strength-adjusted comparison is reported alongside.
